description: Whether an ET1 claim covering any of ISS-002 to ISS-009 is (or will be) in time, given the ACAS Early Conciliation precondition. A threshold, jurisdictional issue that must be resolved before any substantive element below is worth further work.
cause_of_action_or_defence: Threshold/jurisdictional precondition, not itself a cause of action.

elements.element: ET1 presented within the primary 3-month period under ERA 1996 s.111(2)(a) (unfair dismissal, s.103A automatic unfair dismissal, and s.47B/s.48 whistleblowing detriment), or such further period as the Tribunal considers reasonable under s.111(2)(b), as extended by the ACAS EC stop-the-clock/one-month-extension mechanism in ERA 1996 s.207B.
elements.standard: Primary period assessed on the facts as they stand; the 'not reasonably practicable' limb under s.111(2)(b) requires more than a bare balance-of-probabilities showing - a fact-specific reasonableness test.
evidence_missing: Actual EDT from a termination/dismissal letter or HR record
The ACAS EC certificate itself (states both Day A and Day B)
The actual date the ET1 was, or will be, presented - not stated anywhere in the facts supplied
elements.opposition_position: Not yet known - no ET3 or Respondent position exists in this matter.

elements.element: ET1 presented within the primary 3-month period, or such other period as the Tribunal thinks just and equitable, under Equality Act 2010 s.123, for the discrimination-based heads (ISS-005 to ISS-008) - assessed independently of the ERA analysis above since the two statutes apply materially different tests.
elements.standard: Just and equitable to extend - a wider discretion than the unfair dismissal 'reasonably practicable' test.
evidence_missing: Same primary documents as the element above

Identification of the specific EqA 'act complained of' and its date, which may not be the dismissal date at all - e.g. a reasonable-adjustments refusal could be an earlier or continuing act (F-024 gap)

elements.element: Claimant was an employee with the continuity of employment required by ERA 1996 s.108 (currently 2 years for most claims) to bring an ordinary unfair dismissal complaint.
evidence_missing: Contract of employment / statement of terms
HR service record confirming start date and continuity

elements.element: Claimant was dismissed within the meaning of ERA 1996 s.95.
evidence_missing: Termination documentation (exists per F-019 but content not seen)
elements.opposition_position: Not yet known - dismissal is not disputed on the facts as supplied.

elements.element: Respondent shows the reason (or principal reason) for dismissal was one of the potentially fair reasons in ERA 1996 s.98(1)-(2) (capability, conduct, redundancy, statutory restriction, or some other substantial reason).
evidence_missing: Termination documentation actually stating the reason
Disciplinary process outcome letter

elements.element: If a potentially fair reason is shown, dismissal was fair in all the circumstances under ERA 1996 s.98(4) - within the range of reasonable responses, including a reasonable investigation and ACAS Code-compliant procedure.
elements.standard: Range of reasonable responses, assessed against the underlying facts on the balance of probabilities.
evidence_missing: Full disciplinary process file (investigation report, hearing minutes, outcome/appeal letters)
Content of the contradictory internal emails (F-013/F-014), which may bear on whether a reasonable investigation was carried out

description: Automatic unfair dismissal for making a protected disclosure.
cause_of_action_or_defence: Cause of action - ERA 1996 s.103A. No qualifying period of service required, unlike ISS-002.

elements.element: Claimant made one or more qualifying disclosures under ERA 1996 s.43B that are also protected disclosures under ss.43A, 43C-43H (made to the employer or another proper recipient).
evidence_missing: The disclosure(s) themselves - document, email, or recorded conversation with content, recipient, and date
Any grievance or internal report referencing the disclosure

elements.element: The reason (or principal reason) for dismissal was that the claimant made a protected disclosure.
evidence_missing: Chronology placing the disclosure(s) before the disciplinary process/dismissal (see chronology/chronology_gaps.md)
Termination documentation's stated reason, to compare against the reason claimant alleges

cause_of_action_or_defence: Cause of action - ERA 1996 s.47B, remedy/burden mechanics in s.48.

elements.element: Claimant made a protected disclosure (shared element with ISS-003).
evidence_missing: Same as ISS-003 first element

elements.element: Claimant was subjected to a detriment (short of dismissal - e.g. the disciplinary process itself, adverse treatment reflected in the contradictory emails) by the employer or a co-worker.
evidence_missing: Specific detrimental acts identified and dated
Content of the contradictory emails (F-013/F-014)

elements.element: The protected disclosure was a ground for the detriment - once claimant shows disclosure plus detriment, ERA 1996 s.48(2) places the burden on the Respondent to show the disclosure was not a ground for the treatment.
elements.standard: Materially influenced the treatment - a lower threshold than s.103A's 'sole or principal reason'.
evidence_missing: Respondent's contemporaneous rationale for the disciplinary process and any adverse treatment

description: Threshold disability status - a gateway issue for ISS-006 and ISS-007, both of which fail if this element is not made out.
cause_of_action_or_defence: Gateway element, not itself a free-standing cause of action - Equality Act 2010 s.6, Sch 1.

elements.element: Claimant has a physical or mental impairment which has a substantial and long-term adverse effect on their ability to carry out normal day-to-day activities.
evidence_missing: Medical/OH evidence establishing diagnosis, substantiality, and longevity of effect (content of the OH material at F-015/F-016 has not been seen)
Sickness absence pattern showing duration (content of F-017/F-018 has not been seen)
Any GP/consultant evidence

cause_of_action_or_defence: Cause of action - Equality Act 2010 s.15. Gated by ISS-005.

elements.element: Claimant was subjected to unfavourable treatment (e.g. disciplinary action, dismissal).
evidence_missing: Specifics of the unfavourable treatment and its stated rationale

elements.element: The unfavourable treatment was because of something arising in consequence of the claimant's disability (e.g. disability-related sickness absence triggering the disciplinary process).
elements.standard: Balance of probabilities on the initial facts, then the Equality Act 2010 s.136 burden-shift applies (see ISS-006 third element).
evidence_missing: Whether the disciplinary process was absence-related or conduct-related at all - the stated reason for dismissal is not known (F-020)

elements.element: Respondent knew, or could reasonably have been expected to know, of the disability (s.15(2) knowledge defence).
evidence_missing: OH reports actually notifying the employer of the condition and its effects

elements.element: If unfavourable treatment and the disability-connection are shown, Respondent shows the treatment was a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim (objective justification).
evidence_missing: Respondent's stated aim and evidence of proportionality - nothing supplied

cause_of_action_or_defence: Cause of action - Equality Act 2010 ss.20-21. Gated by ISS-005.

elements.element: A provision, criterion or practice (PCP) applied by the Respondent (or a physical feature, or absence of an auxiliary aid) put the claimant at a substantial disadvantage compared with persons who are not disabled.
evidence_missing: Identification of the actual PCP and the actual adjustment(s) sought - not stated at all (F-024)

elements.element: Respondent knew or ought reasonably to have known both of the disability and of the substantial disadvantage.
evidence_missing: Same OH/HR notification evidence as ISS-006 third element

elements.element: Respondent failed to take such steps as it was reasonable to take to avoid the disadvantage.
elements.standard: Balance of probabilities / reasonableness, following the Equality Act 2010 s.136 burden-shift once the claimant shows facts from which a contravention could be found.
evidence_missing: Any adjustment request, OH recommendation, and Respondent's response to it - none supplied

cause_of_action_or_defence: Cause of action - Equality Act 2010 s.27.

elements.element: Claimant did a protected act under s.27(2) (e.g. bringing discrimination proceedings, giving evidence, making an allegation of a contravention of the Equality Act 2010), or the Respondent believed the claimant had done or might do a protected act.
evidence_missing: Identification of the specific protected act relied on - not stated at all (F-023)

elements.element: Respondent subjected the claimant to a detriment because of the protected act (or the belief about it).
elements.standard: Balance of probabilities on the initial facts, then the Equality Act 2010 s.136 burden-shift.
evidence_missing: Causal link evidence between the protected act and the disciplinary process/dismissal

description: Procedural unfairness - relevant to the ERA 1996 s.98(4) fairness assessment and to remedy (Polkey deduction; ACAS Code uplift). Not a free-standing cause of action.
cause_of_action_or_defence: Remedy/fairness-assessment issue, not a cause of action - relevant to ISS-002 and to quantum across the unfair dismissal heads.

elements.element: Whether the Respondent followed a fair procedure, assessed against the ACAS Code of Practice 1 on Disciplinary and Grievance Procedures.
elements.standard: Balance of probabilities as to what was actually done.
evidence_missing: Full disciplinary process file - same gap as ISS-002 fourth element

elements.element: If procedure was unfair, whether and to what percentage compensation should be reduced for the chance dismissal would have occurred anyway with a fair procedure (Polkey).
elements.standard: Percentage-chance assessment, with the underlying facts found on the balance of probabilities.
evidence_missing: Cannot be assessed until the true reason for dismissal (F-020) and the disciplinary file are known

elements.element: If the Respondent unreasonably failed to comply with the ACAS Code, an uplift of up to 25% may be applied to compensation under the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992 s.207A.
elements.standard: Balance of probabilities as to non-compliance, then a percentage judgment.
evidence_missing: Same disciplinary file gap
